headline: High-risk shared-workspace and browser/MCP interaction: prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors are plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf ingests workspace files, clipboard, and MCP content by default, while RD-Agent can run browsers and write logs/files. That creates a plausible path where attacker-controlled content from RD-Agent outputs or browsed pages is treated as instructions by Windsurf. The shared filesystem and MCP surfaces make this interaction more than manual copy-paste.
conditions: IF RD-Agent writes untrusted web content or logs into a workspace file that Windsurf reads
IF Windsurf auto-executes or parses MCP/file content as instructions
mitigations: Disable auto-execute in Windsurf
Keep RD-Agent outputs in a separate directory
Strip instructions from browser-derived text before handoff
Require human review before MCP tool calls
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: RD-Agent touches financial reports, competition datasets, execution traces, and logs, and has broad network egress. Windsurf reads and writes workspace files and can use MCP servers, so sensitive data can flow from shared files into a third-party model path. Because both agents can access the same local workspace, leakage is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive RD-Agent artifacts are stored in the same workspace Windsurf opens
IF Windsurf sends workspace contents to its model proxy or MCP server
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Turn off syncing of secret-bearing files
Review which files Windsurf uploads before use
Move credentials out of shared directories
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: RD-Agent supports multiple instances and writes logs/files, while Windsurf has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and shared_state_with_other_instances via local filesystem. Both can mutate the same workspace or git state without an explicit locking mechanism in the profiles, so concurrent edits and repository corruption are plausible by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or workspace directory
IF either agent writes while the other is editing or committing
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout
Pause one agent before the other commits
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Check git status before every write
requires-engineering: add file locks or a coordinator

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent produces research outputs and logs that Windsurf can read from the workspace, so Windsurf may treat A's output as authoritative input. Windsurf has terminal and git actions, but the profiles do not show a mandatory verification step. This is a default interaction pathway, though not enough evidence for high because direct autonomous downstream harm is not explicitly documented.
conditions: IF Windsurf consumes RD-Agent-generated files without independent validation
IF Windsurf uses those outputs to edit code or commit changes
mitigations: Require a second-pass review of RD-Agent outputs
Compare outputs against source artifacts before acting
Disable auto-commit for agent-generated changes
Mark generated files clearly in the workspace
requires-engineering: add validation gates before shell or git actions

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles financial reports and competition datasets, while Windsurf runs as a local editor process with broad workspace access and model-proxy egress. That creates a compliance mismatch risk for sensitive data residency and retention, especially if regulated or contractual data is opened in Windsurf. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling of the same data class.
conditions: IF regulated financial or contractual data is opened in the shared workspace
IF Windsurf uploads that data to its model proxy or retains it in editor logs
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Review retention settings before opening sensitive files
Use redacted copies for agent work
Limit network access during sensitive sessions
requires-engineering: document a data-handling policy for both tools
